alt: Cover slide on cream: a large brass numeral 7 above the title, lines for your pre-arrival message. Below: Send it three days before check-in. Each line answers a question you would otherwise get on arrival day. Direct Ops logo and the word Swipe.

Line 1: The exact address, and a map pin. Guests paste it straight into a taxi app. A pin beats a street name, and saves the call from the wrong gate. Line 2: Check-in time, and the late plan. Say until when someone is at the desk, and exactly what happens after that.

Line 3: How they get in. Reception, key box or door code. One sentence, so nobody stands outside scrolling through old emails. Line 4: Parking. Where it is, how many cars fit, and whether it costs anything.
Line 5: Wi-Fi name and password. It is the first thing they will ask. Put it in writing before they need it. Line 6: One way to reach you. A single number or chat, and the hours a person answers it.
Line 7: One place to eat on the first evening. Somewhere close that is still serving when they arrive. It costs you one sentence, and it is the line that gets a thank-you.

A template to copy, with brackets to fill in. Hello [name], we look forward to welcoming you on [day]. Address: [street and map pin]. Check-in: from [15:00]. After [22:00], your key is in [the key box by the gate]. Parking: [where, how many cars, cost]. Wi-Fi: [network] / [password]. Reach us: [number or chat]. A person answers [08:00 to 22:00]. First evening: [restaurant], [5 minutes on foot], open until [23:00]. See you soon, [your name].
Closing slide on navy: Save it for the next time you rewrite yours. Working notes for small hotels, villas and resorts. Written by people who run them. Direct Ops logo and the handle @getdirectops.

instagram.caption:
Arrival day brings the same handful of questions, every time. You can answer all of them three days early, in one message.

Seven lines to put in it:

1. The exact address, and a map pin
2. Check-in time, and what happens if they arrive late
3. How they get in
4. Parking
5. Wi-Fi name and password
6. One way to reach you, and when a person answers
7. One place to eat on the first evening

Slide 6 is a template you can copy. Save it for the next time you rewrite yours.

What's in your pre-arrival message that isn't on this list?
